intro: If you're coming to Buriram for the football, the racing, or to hike Khao Kradong, and you want somewhere quiet and leafy that feels more like a small resort than a high-rise hotel in the middle of town — Panorama Hotel Buriram is a name a lot of people bring up · It's a 3-star resort-style boutique hotel with rooms laid out around a pool and garden, on Buriram-Prakhon Chai Road in Samet Subdistrict, at the foot of Khao Kradong, about 0.5 km from Khao Kradong Forest Park and about 1 km from Chang Arena · It has 37 freshly decorated, clean rooms, a swimming pool, free parking, and an EV charging point · Prices start at around THB 745/night, with an average rating of about 8.6 across several platforms and 4.3/5 on TripAdvisor.

body.html: Who Panorama Hotel Buriram suits — to put it as simply as possible, this is a hotel for people who want that "small, quiet, leafy resort feel" at a friendly price, not a busy high-rise in the middle of town · It's a 3-star boutique hotel with its room buildings laid out around a pool and garden, so stepping out of your room you're right by the water and the trees — a different atmosphere from your typical in-town hotel · The location is on Buriram-Prakhon Chai Road in Samet Subdistrict, in the zone at the foot of Khao Kradong and close to Chang Arena · Real reviews line up on who fits best here: football fans coming to cheer on Buriram United who want to sleep near the stadium while still getting some peace, racing fans coming for MotoGP or events at Chang International Circuit, travelers hiking Khao Kradong or paying respects at the hilltop chedi who want to stay nearby, and families or couples road-tripping the lower Isan region who need easy parking · Another group that says they're happy here is people who are tired of high-rise hotels and want a low-rise stay that's easy to walk around with no waiting for lifts · On the flip side, if you're after a place right on a walking street where you step out the door into a sea of restaurants and cafes like in the city center, this may not be the fit, because Panorama's main selling points are quiet, cleanliness, and a location near the stadium and Khao Kradong, rather than walkable downtown sightseeing.

Location and getting around — the hotel is located at 168 Moo 9, Buriram-Prakhon Chai Road, Samet Subdistrict, Mueang Buriram District, an edge-of-town zone at the foot of Khao Kradong — not the heart of the commercial district, but still within Mueang district and a short drive into town · What makes a lot of people pick it is how close it is to the key sights on this side of the city: Khao Kradong Forest Park is only about 0.5 km away, and Wat Khao Kradong (Phra Suphat Bophit / the replica Buddha's footprint) is just a few hundred meters away, an easy walk or drive up for views over Buriram from the hilltop · As for Chang Arena (Buriram United's home ground), it's about 1 km away, just a few minutes' drive — great for football fans who don't want to sleep far from the stadium · Chang International Circuit (the racetrack) is a bit further out toward the edge of town, about a 10–15 min drive · For longer trips: Buriram train station is about 8 km away, a few minutes' drive, and Buriram Airport (BFV) is about 40 km away, around an hour's drive · The honest caveat is that this kind of location "can't be walked" the way an in-town hotel can — the area around the hotel is fairly quiet, and restaurants and convenience stores aren't right by the door, so if you're not driving yourself, have the Grab app or a taxi number ready and plan your meals a little ahead · But for people who drive, this location is a great fit, because it's close to the stadium and Khao Kradong, and town isn't far either.

"Came to cheer at Chang Arena and picked this place because it's only a few minutes' drive to the stadium · The hotel is really quiet, the rooms are spotless like new, there's a pool and garden to walk around, parking is easy, and it's far cheaper than I expected — genuinely good value."

Room types and decor — Panorama Hotel Buriram has 37 rooms in several types, arranged as low-rise buildings around the pool and garden, so getting in and out of your room is easy with no waiting for a lift · The main rooms break down into Standard Twin (two single beds), Standard Double/King (a large bed) and rooms for three, suiting couples, friends traveling together, and small families alike · The decor is contemporary in an easy-on-the-eye palette, leaning on cleanliness and simplicity in keeping with the hotel's boutique concept · In-room amenities include air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge/minibar, tea- and coffee-making facilities, drinking water, and free Wi-Fi · Bathrooms are shower-type with basic toiletries provided · What real reviews praise most consistently is how clean and fresh the rooms are — many use the phrase "spotless" and say it feels like staying in a room that's just been renovated, with comfortable beds and air conditioning that's cool enough on a normal night · That said, to be straight with you, some reviews note a few things about the rooms: some say the lighting in the room is fairly dim, so reading or putting on makeup may not be bright enough, there are few power outlets, so if you're coming as a group with lots of devices to charge you may want to bring your own power strip, and in some rooms at certain times the air conditioning doesn't get cold enough on really hot days · These are things a little preparation can handle, and they don't erase the strengths in cleanliness and atmosphere that many people loved.

Facilities and the pool — the charm that sets Panorama apart from similarly priced hotels in Buriram is its resort-style layout around the pool and garden · There's a small outdoor swimming pool in the central area, perfect for a cool-down after hiking Khao Kradong or coming back from the football, with a pond and trees around it that keep the atmosphere leafy and cool — many reviews say it feels quieter and more relaxing than they'd expect at this price · A clear advantage for drivers is the free on-site parking, which is wide and convenient, ideal for people road-tripping the lower Isan region or coming for an event at the stadium · And interesting for this day and age, the hotel has an electric-vehicle (EV) charger, still not easy to find at upcountry stays in this price range, a real plus for people driving an EV · There's also free Wi-Fi, laundry service, and common areas to sit and relax · To be straight about it, this is a small boutique hotel, so there's no full gym or spa, and the pool is a small one for cooling off rather than serious lap swimming · Another thing reviews flag is that, being low-rise buildings, there's no lift, so if your bags are heavy, ask for a ground-floor room or be ready to carry things up the stairs · Overall the strength here is the atmosphere and a complete set of the basics at a budget price, rather than luxury facilities.

Food and dining — food is one point worth getting clear on before you book, because the information from each platform doesn't quite line up · Some sources say certain packages include breakfast, while other platforms don't list breakfast as a standard service, and there are a few reviews that say "I booked thinking breakfast was included but it turned out there wasn't any" · So the most honest advice is, when booking, check clearly whether the package you choose includes breakfast, and if you want breakfast at the hotel, confirm with the hotel once more to avoid any misunderstanding · The upside of the location is that, even though it's not in the city center, you can drive into central Buriram to find food in not much time — Isan restaurants, noodles, grilled food, cafes, and an evening market · On top of that, on match or event days there are plenty of restaurants and shops around Chang Arena to choose from · So a lot of people stay at Panorama for the quiet and the parking, then drive out to hunt down good food in town or around the stadium for each meal, which fits a style of using the hotel as a base to rest · In short, in-hotel food isn't the main selling point here, but the location makes up for it well if you have a car.

Service — service is another point that draws fairly consistent praise in real reviews · Many staff are described as friendly, smiling, attentive, and helpful, whether with check-in and check-out, recommending places to visit like Khao Kradong, or helping coordinate various things · Being a small hotel, looking after guests feels closer and more personal than at a big hotel, and many reviews say they were impressed by the team's effort and felt warmly welcomed · This fits the hotel's concept, which leans on simplicity and a good feeling during your stay · In fairness, because it's a small team, when the hotel is full (such as on big match days or event days at the stadium) service can slow down a little at times with the volume of guests, but overall service is a strength that lifts the stay above its price, and one reason the service score sits in good territory.

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — pulling together Trip.com, Agoda, Wongnai and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: rooms so clean and fresh that many use the word "spotless", a quiet, leafy resort-style atmosphere around the pool, a location near Chang Arena and Khao Kradong that's a few minutes' drive away, wide free parking with an EV charger, friendly and attentive staff, and excellent value for what you get · On the caveat side: the things mentioned most often are fairly dim lighting in the room and few power outlets, air conditioning in some rooms at certain times not getting cold enough on really hot days, no lift because they're low-rise buildings (heavy bags should ask for a ground-floor room), confusion over whether breakfast is included or not, and a quiet location that makes walking to find a restaurant without a car inconvenient · A few reviews mention some minor insects at certain times, which is something you can run into at garden stays close to nature and can usually be sorted by telling the hotel · Overall these criticisms are details you can manage by preparing and setting your expectations right, rather than big problems, so it's no surprise the overall score still sits in good territory and many say they'd come back again.

"The room was super clean like it had just been redone, the atmosphere is quiet, really good for resting, and the staff are lovely · The only knocks are that the lighting in the room is a bit dark and there are a few too few outlets — next time I'll bring my own power strip — but overall it's great value for the price."

Price comparison and value — the starting price for a Standard room is around THB 745/night in the regular price range, with an average around THB 1,000/night depending on the season and platform · Prices can climb during big events like key Buriram United home matches or racing events at Chang International Circuit, when the whole town fills up fast · Compared with other Buriram hotels, this price is excellent value among the stays near the stadium, especially once you factor in the free parking, EV charger, swimming pool, and the garden-around-a-pool atmosphere you won't find in a high-rise hotel at the same price · Compared with the upscale hotels right by the stadium like Amari Buriram United or Modena by Fraser Buriram, which cost more and have more facilities, Panorama suits people who are watching their budget, want quiet, and aren't fussed about a gym/spa · And compared with guesthouses or the cheapest stays in town, this place feels like it gives you "atmosphere and cleanliness beyond the price" · In short, it's a balanced choice between price, a location near the stadium, and a restful atmosphere, suited to people coming for the football, the racing, or hiking Khao Kradong by car.

What to know before you book — a few things will make your stay go more smoothly · One, if you drive yourself, this is one of the hotel's big advantages — make full use of the free parking and plan your routes to Chang Arena, Khao Kradong, Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam from here easily, and EV drivers can use the charger at the hotel · Two, check clearly whether the package you book includes breakfast, because the information differs by platform, and if you want breakfast at the hotel, confirm with the hotel once more · Three, if your bags are heavy or stairs aren't easy for you, ask for a ground-floor room when you book, because the low-rise buildings have no lift · Four, if you need several charging outlets or like a bright room, bring a power strip and a small portable light just in case, because reviews say the lighting in the room is fairly dim and there are few outlets · Five, during big events (home matches or racing events) the whole town fills up fast and prices climb, so book several weeks to several months ahead and pick free cancellation first if your plans aren't certain · Six, because the location is fairly quiet, if you don't have a car, have the Grab app or a taxi number ready and plan your meals and trips into town ahead.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Panorama Hotel Buriram is the best fit for people who want to stay near Chang Arena and Khao Kradong in a quiet, resort-style atmosphere around a pool, on a manageable budget · Rooms clean like new, a leafy garden setting, free parking, an EV charger, and friendly staff make it a good-value, likeable choice for football fans, racing fans, and travelers driving through the lower Isan region · If you're looking for a stay in the city center where you step out the door into a sea of restaurants and cafes, or you want the full set of big-hotel facilities — lift, gym, and spa — this may not be the answer, and you should consider an in-town hotel or a higher-tier one instead · But for a trip built around the football, the racing, or hiking Khao Kradong by car, where you want quiet, cleanliness, and a location near the stadium at a friendly price — Panorama Hotel Buriram answers that need nicely.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Panorama Hotel Buriram

faq.q: Where is Panorama Hotel Buriram · what's nearby?
faq.a: The hotel is at 168 Moo 9, Buriram-Prakhon Chai Road, Samet Subdistrict, Mueang Buriram District, in the zone at the foot of Khao Kradong · Wat Khao Kradong is just about 0.2 km away, Khao Kradong Forest Park about 0.5 km, and Chang Arena about 1 km · Chang International Circuit is about a 10–15 min drive, Buriram train station about 8 km, and Buriram Airport (BFV) about 40 km (~1 hr drive).

faq.q: How much does Panorama Hotel Buriram cost to start · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 745/night for a Standard room (average around THB 1,000) · There are Standard Double/King, Standard Twin, rooms for 3, and Deluxe rooms · During big events like Buriram United home matches or racing events at Chang, prices climb and rooms fill up fast, so compare several platforms and book ahead.

faq.q: Does the hotel have a swimming pool, parking, and an EV charger?
faq.a: There's a small outdoor swimming pool in a garden-around-a-pool setting, perfect for cooling off · There's free on-site parking, wide and convenient, ideal for people driving through the lower Isan region · And there's an electric-vehicle (EV) charging point, still not easy to find at upcountry stays in this price range · Free Wi-Fi throughout · Because they're low-rise buildings there's no lift, so heavy bags should ask for a ground-floor room.

faq.q: Who does Panorama Hotel Buriram suit?
faq.a: It's a great fit for football fans coming to cheer on Buriram United, racing fans coming for events at Chang, and travelers driving to Khao Kradong and the lower Isan region · Its strengths are a location near the stadium and Khao Kradong, a quiet, leafy atmosphere, clean rooms, free parking, and good value · If you're looking for a stay in the city center where you can walk around, or full big-hotel facilities, an in-town or higher-tier hotel may suit you better.

faq.q: Is breakfast included in the price at Panorama Hotel Buriram?
faq.a: The breakfast information is fairly inconsistent across platforms — some sources say certain packages include breakfast, while other platforms don't list it as a standard service, and a few reviews understood it was included but it turned out it wasn't · The advice is to check clearly when booking whether the package you choose includes breakfast, and if you want breakfast at the hotel, confirm with the hotel once more · The upside is you can drive into town or over to the Chang Arena side to find food in not much time.

faq.q: What are noise and atmosphere like at Panorama Hotel Buriram?
faq.a: Many reviews agree it's quiet and leafy, with its resort-style layout around the pool and garden, good for people who really want to rest · On normal days the atmosphere is very calm, while on big match or event days at Chang it can get a bit livelier with the number of guests · The thing to be ready for is that the lighting in the room is fairly dim and there are few outlets, so if you like a bright room or need to charge several devices, we recommend bringing a power strip and a small portable light just in case.
